design.affected_system: rights-preserving compliance assistance, incentives, inspections, and enforcement
alternatives: advance high-risk work within verified feasible windows for compliance notice, assistance, inspection, and appeal schedule
use rolling risk and capacity updates to reschedule compliance notice, assistance, inspection, and appeal schedule
pair rights, deadline, dependency, capacity, and burden-aware scheduling with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Eligibility, notice, awareness, capability, action, inspection, violation, sanction, and outcome remain distinct.
No behavioral score automatically triggers enforcement, benefit denial, or coercive action.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: continue the fixed operating calendar for compliance notice, assistance, inspection, and appeal schedule.

constraints.description: The compliance, incentives, and behavioral policy schedule must respect declared labor, access, sequencing, notice, and completion windows.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
design.decision_owner: regulatory operations director and behavioral insights lead
design.decision_question: When should notice, support, cure periods, inspection, decision, appeal, and follow-up occur?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The compliance, incentives, and behavioral policy schedule must respect declared labor, access, sequencing, notice, and completion windows.
independence_key.decision_object: compliance notice, assistance, inspection, and appeal schedule
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for compliance notice, assistance, inspection, and appeal schedule passes documented checks for effective dates, time zones, calendars, lead times, completion semantics, and update cadence.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: rights, deadline, dependency, capacity, and burden-aware scheduling
independence_key.primary_outcome: case-days outside lawful notice, assistance, and review windows

design.intended_claim: A versioned schedule design for comparing declared alternatives affecting compliance notice, assistance, inspection, and appeal schedule, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: case-days outside lawful notice, assistance, and review windows
distributional gap in case-days outside lawful notice, assistance, and review windows
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not call scheduled notice delivered, understood, lawful, cured, inspected, or adjudicated.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for compliance notice, assistance, inspection, and appeal schedule passes documented checks for effective dates, time zones, calendars, lead times, completion semantics, and update cadence.

design.title: Schedule notices, assistance, inspections, and appeals
transportability_risks: Law, administrative burden, trust, incentives, capability, enforcement, and baseline behavior differ.
Observed compliance may reflect detection and documentation rather than underlying behavior.

family.affected_system: rights-preserving compliance assistance, incentives, inspections, and enforcement
claim_boundary: Area and administrative differences do not establish discrimination, preferences, or individual behavior.
Behavioral and allocation designs require rights, accessibility, privacy, and non-coercion review.
Causal, fairness, adoption, and welfare claims require direct outcomes and independent governance evidence.
family.decision_owner: regulatory operations director and behavioral insights lead
family.description: Eight decisions for process diagnosis, workload forecasting, policy portfolios, service siting, support allocation, contact scheduling, behavior stress, and incentive evaluation.
family.title: Compliance, incentives, and behavioral policy

library_claim_boundary: The catalog contains 240 decision designs, not 240 city executions.
Exactly twelve designs map to existing Tier-D reference templates; 228 remain design-only.
A reference implementation can be an explicit negative release and does not imply impact.
No record claims a city binding, new method, deployment, adoption, or real-user outcome.
Future execution requires source binding, gate passage, and domain, legal, community, and operational review.
